value.name: Governed Operation from Operator Branches
value.description: Make SYNTH govern work on pre-existing operator branches: declare and bind execution branches (ADR-056 --branch/--no-create), anchor and single-write the ceremony ledger (ADR-055: ledger writer, anchor, single writer), and make delivery and abandonment first-class ceremonies (deliver/seal/close/abandon) so finished work, files and history survive the branch lifecycle instead of being stranded or wiped.

evidence.description: Verified: assertExecutionBranch requires mission/<slug>-<id7>; a workspace pinned to arena/c5db653e-synth is denied every mission approval and expedition start, and the mission branch is demanded but never created (only expedition branches are auto-created, at start). Nothing in the taxonomy lets an existing operator branch be bound to governed work. Remedy: ADR-056 --branch/--no-create with a recorded binding.
evidence.snippet: Verified: assertExecutionBranch requires mission/<slug>-<id7>; a workspace pinned to arena/c5db653e-synth is denied every mission approval and expedition start, and the mission branch is demanded but never created (only expedition branches are auto-created, at start). Nothing in the taxonomy lets an existing operator branch be bound to governed work. Remedy: ADR-056 --branch/--no-create with a recorded binding.

evidence.description: Verified with two clean clones (d1/d2): one alignment ceremony in each, then git merge -> all four event-stream segments + canonical-state.json + dependency-records-cache.json conflict, and both clones assigned the same offsets 317/321/326 to different events. Union-by-id with renumbered offsets (337 events) still fails replay: previousHash chains to the last event of the stream (execution-gate.ts:162), so replay reports Hash-chain broken at index 1, chainValid:false, 38 state differences. Consequence: ceremonies need a single writer + an authoritative gate-mediated import, never a text merge; PR merges carrying .synth/** bypass the gate entirely.
